title: Brewers Erase Four-Run Hole to Take 2-0 World Series Lead
dek: Milwaukee beat Tampa Bay 5-4 in Game 2 after trailing 4-0, taking a commanding early series lead. Game 3 is scheduled for Monday night in St. Petersburg.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: A baseball game at Centennial Field in Tallahassee in 1973; an archival illustration, not the 2026 World Series game
image.credit: Roger Linville / Florida Memory, State Library and Archives of Florida

keyPoints: The Brewers beat the Rays 5-4 in Game 2 after falling behind 4-0 in the first inning, according to the AP recap published by ESPN.
Sal Frelick tied the game with a solo home run in the sixth, and Cooper Pratt drove in the go-ahead run in the seventh.
Milwaukee leads the best-of-seven series 2-0; MLB lists Game 3 for Monday, October 26, at 8 p.m. ET in St. Petersburg.
body:
The Milwaukee Brewers turned a four-run first-inning deficit into a 5-4 win over the Tampa Bay Rays on Saturday night, taking a 2-0 lead in the best-of-seven World Series. The comeback followed Milwaukee's one-run win in the opener and left the Rays needing a response at home in Game 3.

## A comeback built inning by inning

Tampa Bay jumped ahead 4-0 in the first, capitalizing on an early defensive error and adding run-scoring singles before Liam Hicks hit a two-run homer. Milwaukee answered with two runs in the bottom half and gradually chipped away. Right fielder Sal Frelick's solo home run in the sixth tied the score at 4-4. Shortstop Cooper Pratt, who had made an early error, delivered the go-ahead RBI single in the seventh, according to the Associated Press recap carried by ESPN.

Milwaukee's pitching staff then held Tampa Bay scoreless for the final eight innings of the game. Abner Uribe earned the win after pitching 1 1/3 hitless innings, and Aaron Ashby closed it by striking out Yandy Díaz with a runner at third in the ninth. The sequence turned a fast start by the Rays into another postseason comeback for a Brewers team that had already recovered from a four-run hole earlier in October.

## The Rays return home

Game 3 is scheduled for Monday, October 26, at 8 p.m. Eastern at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida, according to MLB's schedule. The venue gives Tampa Bay a chance to reset on its home field, but the series position is steep: teams that have gone ahead 2-0 in the World Series have historically converted that advantage at a high rate. The immediate task is narrower than history, though. The Rays need better defense and a way to keep Milwaukee from extending rallies after early leads.

For the Brewers, the first two games reinforce a clear strength: their offense has stayed patient after falling behind, while the bullpen has kept opponents from adding insurance runs. That pattern is not a guarantee of a title, and two games are a small sample. It does, however, give Milwaukee two chances to close out the series at home after Monday's game, and puts the pressure on Tampa Bay to stop the comeback cycle before it becomes the defining story of this Series.
